questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to visit a city with a high educational standard but also have a rich cultural life. I wanted to go to Europe because it was easier with the application and it also helps a lot with the Erasmus gran. Amsterdam perfectly fits all these criteria.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Of course, Covid-19 was still happening and there was also a lockdown while I was in Amsterdam. However, I still had a great time and made new friends and enjoyed my courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Vrije University contacts you several times to remind of the important dates and give great advice. It could not have been any easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A student helper waited for me at the dorm and showed me around. There were also many tutors in bright blue t-shirts guiding us into the auditorium on the very first day of school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy because the university has an agreement with a big student housing cooperation in the NL. I got notifications on how to sign up and also when it was possible to appy for housing. I lived with both international students and Dutch students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is a little bit further away from the university (but Amsterdam is quite small so it is easy to get around). The dormitories away form campus are also much cleaner and were in better conditions. 
If you have your own kitchen and are at least 23 years old you can apply for housing allowance from the government. I got about >200 euro each month. Not all students were aware of this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very easy because the apartments are fully equipped, you get the most basic kitchen equipment, duvets and pillows etc. It was very convenient.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Make sure that the course you are interested in is offered to exchange students. I got merit for some courses which I was not able to register in the end because I did not see that it was not offered to exchange students. 
Vrije University will also inform you about the amount of courses you need to take in each period.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I applied for merit for the chosen courses at my host university. 
When it was time for course registration (it was quite late), Vrije University sent out a notification for course registration. You have a lot of time to apply. 
I was notified that I was not able to register some of the courses because it was not applicable for exchange students. I ended up finding other courses by myself and registered for them. It was quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The VU International team replied very quickly, but it was also possible to e-mail the course coordinators. They were also very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up registering for 2 out of the 5 courses that I initially had merit for because I did not see that some of the courses had pre-requisties or were not offered to exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try to find something (a little bit) outside your track/major but is still relevant. Take advantage of the fact that you are offered some courses that your home university does not have. 
And do not stress too much about the planned courses because you will probably change them anyways due to different unforeseen circumstances. But it is not difficult at all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Research is a very important part of Vrije University so you will gain new insight on this. The students are very skilled and enjoy taking part of the discussions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academia level is very high but it is possible to follow along AND have some free time for going out or do some cultural activities.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is not much one-on-one with the lecturers. It is mostly lectures and and work groups/classroom teaching. Each course had 1-3 assignments. 
They are very much focused on research so you will gain insight into many pharmaceutical methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) ADMET
2) Advanced Molecular Immunology and Cell Biology
3) Drug Target Biochemistry and Signaling
4) Human Cells in Culture
5) Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Drug Target Biochemistry and Signaling and Human Cells in Culture are very useful and relevant if you study Pharmacy/Pharmaceutical Sciences at KU. The lecturers are passionate and skilled.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I got a waste disposal tax of 100 €. I also bought a used bike at Waterlooplein for 80 euro (highly recommended!)
I also ended up getting a museum card where you get free access to several museums in NL. If you visit 3-4 museums the museum card is a good deal.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The generel cost of living is cheaper in Amsterdam compared to Copenhagen. It is cheaper to eat out but also general grocery shopping in the super markets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Corona lockdown hit hard in December but I will still able to have a good time with friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a cinema at Vrije University and there a so many student associations. 
I recommend 3D (look it up on Instagram). They are especially perfect for international students. 
I also recommend joining the sports activities. You can do try outs in the first weeks and sometimes Vrije University also offer some free sports classes because they have health weeks etc :D

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get yourself a museum card

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- visit Albert Cyup market
- visit Brouwerij 't IJ in East/Oost
- attend Amsterdam wine festival 
- go to the museumplein
- visit Vondelpark with friend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The NL is not much different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is quite difficult because they tend to talk to other Dutch students. But if you want to get in contact with Dutch students you can join the groups with Dutch-sounding names when you make the groups for the assignments.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There are so many cultural activities and Amsterdam also offer a lot of excellent restaurants and cafes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Apply for rent allowance if you can.
2) Don't stress out because there WILL be a lot to study, many assignments etc. Make room for having fun also. 
3) Get a bike.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is very big, try to find good study places a part from the Main Building and New Building.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Gaining insight into many new cultures. I got to know many new international students and it is very fun to experience the cultural differences. 
This whole experience also made me appreciate the Danish educational system. We have a big safety net and we do not have to worry as many students from other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to present in front of many people. However, this also made me more comfortable speaking in English now when I am back at KU again and is a part of a research team.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
